prerequisites: Competencies acquired in Technical Drawing subjects of Baccalaureate.

learning_outcomes.text: To know, understand, and apply a body of knowledge on the fundamentals and standardization of industrial engineering drawing, simultaneously fostering the development of spatial ability.
To develop strategies and procedures in the resolution of graphical problems as a means to approach engineering projects.
To use graphical communication among technicians, specifically in creating and interpreting standardized Industrial Engineering Technical Drawings, involving new technologies.
To work in a team, where they develop their knowledge through critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
To foster a favorable attitude towards learning in the profession, showing proactivity, participation, and a spirit of overcoming difficulties in training.
To significantly apply knowledge of basic graphic expression subjects in understanding problematic situations typical of engineering.
To graphically solve problems through analysis, hypothesis formulation, strategy development, and results analysis.
To prepare works, standardized drawings, and written and oral reports using appropriate computer tools. To analyze and correctly express ideas using verbal and graphic language.
To make proposals, analyze contributions from others, discuss ideas, plan, and execute relevant actions in cooperative work.
To show a critical and proactive attitude in performing tasks.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Standardization: Basic elements of industrial drawing standardization.
Fundamentals and Techniques of Representation Systems: Fundamentals of representation systems and procedures or techniques of Descriptive Geometry.
Visualization of Corporeal Forms: External and internal visualization of parts, with all cutting and sectioning procedures.
Surfaces and Their Applications: Classification of curves and surfaces, studying developable ruled surfaces, surfaces of revolution and evolution, performing sections and development of the same.

Dimensioning Networks: Introduction to dimensioning, considering the elements involved in dimensioning. Study of dimensioning processes, ways to dimension dimensions, classification of dimensions, dimensioning systems. All directed to the dimensioning of parts according to the manufacturing and machining process.
Macro and Microgeometric Tolerances: Study of dimensional tolerances, fits, and surface quality, as complementary aspects influencing the functionality and quality level of the finished part.

Standardized Elements and Mechanical Assemblies: Study of all types of joints, both removable and fixed, as well as other types of standardized elements, all aimed at the creation of exploded views of mechanical assemblies.
Computer-Aided Design (CAD): Introduction to CAD systems, structure and analysis of design software. Applications.
assessment_rules: For the Ordinary Call, the written exam component (70%) requires a minimum of 4/10 on the sum of exam scores to pass, and a minimum of 3.5 points on each exercise to average. If these conditions are not met, the maximum grade for the subject is 4 (fail). The CAD laboratory component (30%) is assessed through continuous evaluation via individual assignments (10%) and a team project (20%), and its grade is carried over to the extraordinary call unless the student takes the extraordinary exam. In the Extraordinary Call, the written exam component (70%) again requires a minimum of 4/10 overall and 3.5 points per exercise to average; otherwise, the maximum grade is 4. The CAD laboratory component (30%) is assessed via a written exam covering topics like Axonometric System, assembly drawing, drawing standards, and Solid Edge operations. Students can opt out of continuous assessment by written declaration within 18 weeks.
